# ESLint

[Website](https://eslint.org) |
[Configure ESLint](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure) |
[Rules](https://eslint.org/docs/rules/) |
[Contribute to ESLint](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/contribute) |
[Report Bugs](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/contribute/report-bugs) |
[Code of Conduct](https://eslint.org/conduct) |
[X](https://x.com/geteslint) |
[Discord](https://eslint.org/chat) |
[Mastodon](https://fosstodon.org/@eslint) |
[Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/eslint.org)

ESLint is a tool for identifying and reporting on patterns found in ECMAScript/JavaScript code. In many ways, it is similar to JSLint and JSHint with a few exceptions:

- ESLint uses [Espree](https://github.com/eslint/js/tree/main/packages/espree) for JavaScript parsing.
- ESLint uses an AST to evaluate patterns in code.
- ESLint is completely pluggable, every single rule is a plugin and you can add more at runtime.

ESLint is a tool for identifying and reporting on patterns found in ECMAScript/JavaScript code, with the goal of making code more consistent and avoiding bugs.

ESLint is completely pluggable. Every single rule is a plugin and you can add more at runtime. You can also add community plugins, configurations, and parsers to extend the functionality of ESLint.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
